summary: Pweto territory (Haut-Katanga), on Lake Mweru and the Zambian border, is state-held. Pweto and Kilwa towns and the southern/lakeside villages are under ordinary state administration with PNC policing and FARDC posts. The north of the territory (Mwenge chefferie on the Pweto-Mwenge axis, bordering Mitwaba and Moba) suffers persistent Mai-Mai Kata Katanga activity (22,000 displaced from Kasongo-Kamulumbi in 2023; April 2026 protection mission flags instability amplified by the MDKC incursion in Mitwaba); it is assessed as FARDC-held, contested in Kasongo-Kamulumbi. No source shows a militia durably governing localities in the unit as of late 2026.

zones.description: Pweto town (territory HQ, Lake Mweru / Luvua outlet, Zambian border)
zones.evidence: Territorial seat under state administration with PNC and an FARDC garrison; it receives IDPs from Mwenge and neighbouring Mitwaba/Moba, i.e. it is treated as a safe zone. Mai-Mai Kata Katanga activity in 2023-2026 is reported in the rural north (Pweto-Mwenge axis), not in the town.

zones.description: Kilwa city (Lake Mweru) and its health-area neighbourhoods (Kilwa, Kapufi, Mulangale, Kamutrombe, Katenge)
zones.evidence: State-held lakeside town with PNC and FARDC; the 15 Aug 2024 incident (about ten killed) was security forces firing on a crowd they took for Kata Katanga militiamen, not a militia takeover. No reports of an armed group holding the town in 2025-2026.

zones.description: Kasongo-Kamulumbi groupement, northwestern Mwenge chefferie (Katubilwa, Kazeba, Dilenda, Sylvain, Kasongo Kamulumbi) toward Mitwaba/Moba
zones.evidence: About 22,000 people fled this groupement in May-Nov 2023 due to Katangese Mai-Mai (FPK) insecurity; an April 2026 protection mission reports persistent instability on the Pweto-Mwenge axis from Mai-Mai Kata Katanga activism and the MDKC incursion in adjacent Mitwaba (March 2026). State control is assessed as FARDC-led and contested; no source shows the militia governing villages.

zones.description: Rest of Mwenge chefferie on the Pweto-Mwenge axis: Mwenge, Kasama groupement (IDP host area), Kisaba, Kalenge, Kabawe, Madimba, Kivungu, Mpongo
zones.evidence: Kasama groupement hosts IDPs from Kasongo-Kamulumbi and Moba, and the Pweto-Mwenge axis is a 2026 protection concern with FARDC deployed; Mai-Mai Kata Katanga raids are reported but the state keeps a presence. The army is assumed the main force given the operational context.

zones.description: Southern and eastern Pweto health zone: Kamakanga, Kisakana/Mumbalanga, Katonta, Kakonona, Kapata/Mwashi, Kapulo mine area, Kizabi, Mwela, Kinkalangu (Lake Mweru/Luvua shore)
zones.evidence: No reports of armed-group control in these villages near Pweto town and along the lake/Luvua in 2025-2026; FARDC units are posted along the roads (e.g. the May 2026 shooting by soldiers in the Pweto area). Assessed as ordinary state presence.

zones.description: Rural Kilwa health zone (Lukonzolwa/Sotala, Dubie/Mansanga, Lwanza/Kabulembe, Lusalala, Kasolo, Dikulushi, Kabangu, Mubanga, Kyaka, Mukupa/Kankumbwa, Mulinde) plus Kilwa-area villages in Mufunga-Sampwe and Kashobwe health zones
zones.evidence: No reported armed-group presence in the Kilwa hinterland in 2025-2026; Bakata Katanga activity is concentrated in Mitwaba, Malemba-Nkulu, Manono/Moba and the far north of Pweto. FARDC soldiers were posted at Kabulembe (May 2026 shooting). Default state presence.
